sites.residue_label: C-terminal ectodomain (last exon, before GPI signal)
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by V5 immunostaining in fixed neurons; no functional assay reported for the tagged endogenous protein.
sites.rationale: L5–L6 report endogenous CRISPR tagging of Cntn1 with smFP-V5 inserted into the 'last exon'; surface display is confirmed by V5 immunostaining. For a GPI-anchored protein the insertion must lie upstream of the GPI signal to survive processing, placing it in the C-terminal ectodomain. No specific residue number is given in the ledger, so the site is recorded at region level only; a junction cannot be invented. The smFP-V5 is a large tag, but the evidence establishes that this region of the ectodomain tolerates insertion. CRISPR-mediated endogenous knock-in of smFP-V5 (spaghetti-monster fluorescent protein with V5 tags) into the last exon of Cntn1 via AAV-delivered Cas9 and sgRNA in DIV0 rat hippocampal neurons; V5 immunostaining two weeks post-transduction confirms surface display of the endogenously tagged protein.

sources.claim: To endogenously label these 23 cell surface proteins, we generated two adeno-associated viruses (AAV) to transduce cultured DIV 0 rat hippocampal neurons with (1) Cas9 and (2) a gene specific single guide RNA (sgRNA), a sgRNA that recognizes donor recognition sites (DRS) flanking spaghetti monster fluorescent protein with V5 tags (smFP-V5), and smFP-V5 (Fig. 5b ).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by immunostaining and AIS colocalisation with β4 spectrin in vitro and in vivo; no quantitative functional assay (e.g. binding, conduction) reported for the tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: CNTN1 is a GPI-anchored protein with no transmembrane or cytoplasmic domain; the pipeline topology confirms EXTRACELLULAR 21–1018 with signal peptide 1–20. Because the C-terminal GPI signal (~last 20–30 aa) is cleaved during GPI attachment, a C-terminal tag would be lost; the only stable extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus at residue 21. The 'Cntn1-myc' construct shows confirmed surface display, so the Myc tag must reside after the signal-peptide cleavage site, i.e. insert_after_residue = 20. Python confirms residue 20 = A and residue 21 = E, consistent with the canonical sequence. AAV-delivered Cntn1-myc overexpression construct expressed in cultured hippocampal neurons and in vivo in cortical neurons; the Myc-tagged full-length protein is detected at the cell surface (AIS), colocalising with β4 spectrin.

sources.claim: Scale bar, 10 μm. d, Schematic of the Cntn1-myc overexpression vector used for in vitro and in vivo infection of neurons. e, Transduction of cultured hippocampal neurons using AAV to express Myc-tagged Cntn1.

literature_notes: CNTN1 is a GPI-anchored cell-adhesion molecule with no transmembrane or cytoplasmic domain (topology: SIGNAL 1–20, EXTRACELLULAR 21–1018). All eight ledger lines come from two papers (PMC10028829 and PMC10603070). L1–L4 and L7–L8 all describe the same 'Cntn1-myc' overexpression construct; L5–L6 describe the smFP-V5 endogenous knock-in. Neither paper states a residue number for the tag junction. For 'Cntn1-myc', because the C-terminal GPI signal is cleaved during GPI attachment, the only extracellular terminus that can carry a surface-displayed tag is the mature N-terminus (after residue 20); the position is therefore topology_derived. For the smFP-V5 'last exon' insertion, surface display is confirmed but no residue is given, so the site is recorded at region level. No ledger line names a specific residue, so no 'validated' site can be reported. The smFP-V5 tag is far larger than the ~13–23 aa ALFA-class tags requested, but the evidence still establishes regional tolerance for insertion in the C-terminal ectodomain.
